laws.penalty: Commercial surf instruction without registration: fines up to ¥1,000,000; surfing in prohibited swimming zone: ¥30,000 fine
exceptions: Surf competitions with coast guard coordination and temporary zone closures

quiz.q: What minimum separation must kitesurfers maintain from swimmers at Okinawan beaches?
quiz.explanation: Kitesurfers must maintain 100 metres separation from designated swimming areas in Okinawa — the kite's large radius of motion and rapid speed make closer proximity dangerous to swimmers.

laws.title: Ocean Plastic Waste — Okinawa Beach Cleanup Obligations
laws.subtitle: Marine plastic debris a major Okinawa environmental challenge
laws.fullDescription: Okinawa's beaches — particularly on the Japan Sea-facing northern coasts — accumulate significant ocean plastic debris from China, Korea, and the wider Pacific. Under Japan's Act on Promotion of Marine Plastic Litter Measures (海洋プラスチックごみ対策促進法, 2021), local governments must develop marine litter action plans. Okinawa Prefecture organises beach cleanup programmes and tracks debris origin. Deliberate littering into ocean or coastal areas carries enhanced penalties under Waste Management Law.
laws.penalty: Deliberate ocean littering: up to ¥5,000,000 fine under Waste Management Law; ocean dumping from vessels: Criminal penalties under London Protocol implementing legislation
exceptions: Fishing gear lost in storms is not criminal — reporting obligations apply for retrieval
laws.sourceLabel: Ministry of Environment — Marine Plastic Litter Act

quiz.q: From where does much of the ocean plastic debris accumulating on Okinawa's northern beaches originate?
options: Hawaii and the Great Pacific Garbage Patch
China, Korea, and the wider Pacific via ocean currents
quiz.explanation: Okinawa's northern beaches accumulate plastic debris carried by ocean currents from China, Korea, and the broader Pacific — a transnational environmental problem requiring international cooperation.

laws.title: Shuri Castle Reconstruction Public Participation
laws.subtitle: Historic reconstruction involving public donations and oversight
laws.fullDescription: The Shuri Castle reconstruction (ongoing since the 2019 fire) is funded by national and prefectural government plus public donations (募金) — which exceeded ¥4.8 billion by 2024. The reconstruction is governed by an Advisory Committee including historians, cultural property experts, and community representatives. Authentic traditional building methods (木工技術) are being used to recreate the original Ryukyuan royal palace using Okinawan timber. The project is expected to complete the main hall by 2026.
laws.penalty: Fraudulent Shuri Castle donation solicitations: fraud charges up to 10 years; diversion of designated restoration funds: criminal breach of trust

quiz.q: How much did public donations for Shuri Castle's reconstruction exceed by 2024?
quiz.explanation: Public donations for Shuri Castle's reconstruction exceeded ¥4.8 billion by 2024 — reflecting the castle's deep importance to Okinawan identity and Japanese national heritage.

laws.title: Aquarium Species Import — Okinawa Coral Fish Trade
laws.subtitle: CITES controls on ornamental fish collection
laws.fullDescription: Okinawa's reefs support a major ornamental fish collection industry — with species including Nemo-type clownfish (カクレクマノミ), mandarin fish, and various wrasse sought by global aquarium trade. CITES Appendix II restrictions apply to certain reef fish and coral species. Japan's Wildlife Protection Act and CITES implementing legislation require export permits for controlled species and prohibit collection from Marine Protected Area cores. Captive-bred clownfish have largely replaced wild collection for domestic sales since 'Finding Nemo' demand spikes.
laws.penalty: Illegal wild collection of CITES-listed reef fish: up to 5 years imprisonment; export without permit: same penalties
exceptions: Captive-bred specimens with documented provenance
laws.sourceLabel: Ministry of Environment — CITES Marine Species

quiz.q: What film drove a massive spike in demand for Okinawa's clownfish (カクレクマノミ) — prompting a shift to captive breeding?
quiz.explanation: Pixar's 'Finding Nemo' (2003) triggered a global demand spike for clownfish (Amphiprion ocellaris) — threatening wild populations until the aquarium industry shifted to captive breeding to meet demand.

laws.title: Traditional Okinawan Medicine — Chinpi and Herb Rules
laws.subtitle: Traditional plant remedies regulated as food or quasi-pharmaceutical
laws.fullDescription: Okinawa's traditional medicine uses indigenous plants including turmeric (ウコン, ukon), chinpi (陳皮, dried citrus peel), and various tropical herbs. These products are regulated as foods or 'food with functional claims' (機能性表示食品) under the Food Labelling Act — they cannot claim to cure diseases. The thriving turmeric (ukon) industry in Okinawa (Yomitan Village is the production centre) must clearly distinguish food from pharmaceutical claims. Imported tropical herbs must clear phytosanitary inspection.
laws.penalty: Medical claims on food products without PMDA approval: up to 2 years imprisonment under Pharmaceutical Affairs Law
exceptions: General food health claims within approved functional claim categories
laws.sourceLabel: Consumer Affairs Agency — Functional Food Claims

quiz.q: What Okinawan herb — a bright yellow spice — is the centre of a major production industry in Yomitan Village?
quiz.explanation: Turmeric (ukon, ウコン) production is centred in Yomitan Village, Okinawa — marketed for liver health benefits, with Okinawa producing the majority of Japan's domestically grown turmeric.

laws.title: US Base Construction Employment Rules
laws.subtitle: Japanese workers at US bases subject to hybrid employment law
laws.fullDescription: Approximately 9,000 Japanese nationals work at US military bases in Okinawa — employed by the US Forces through the Japan-US Labour Agreement. These workers are subject to Japanese labour law for core protections (minimum wage, working hours, safety) but US military operating procedures for workplace rules. The Japan-US Labour Committee (日米合同委員会労働分科会) resolves disputes. Base workers are eligible for Japan's employment insurance and social security systems.
laws.penalty: Base operators (US military) violating Japanese labour law minimums for Japanese employees: diplomatic complaints → Labour Agreement dispute resolution
exceptions: US military personnel themselves are not subject to Japanese labour law
laws.sourceLabel: Ministry of Health — Japan-US Labour Agreement

quiz.q: Approximately how many Japanese nationals work at US military bases in Okinawa?
quiz.explanation: Approximately 9,000 Japanese nationals are employed at US military bases in Okinawa — subject to Japanese labour law for core protections under the Japan-US Labour Agreement.

laws.title: Kumiodori Classical Drama — UNESCO Heritage
laws.subtitle: Ryukyuan classical opera inscribed as UNESCO Intangible Heritage
laws.fullDescription: Kumiodori (組踊) — Okinawa's classical theatrical form combining dance, music, and poetry, created by Tamagusuku Chokun in 1719 for reception of Chinese imperial envoys — is inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage Representative List (2010). Performers train for over 10 years under master teachers of the National Theatre Okinawa (国立劇場おきなわ). Kumiodori uses Okinawan language (uchinaaguchi) and traditional costume — its preservation is threatened by the declining number of Okinawan language speakers.
laws.penalty: Damage to Kumiodori traditional costume and instruments (National Important Cultural Property designation): up to 5 years; fraudulent performance certification: fraud charges
exceptions: Student training performances and non-commercial educational presentations

quiz.q: For what occasion was Kumiodori classical drama created in 1719?
options: Celebration of the Ryukyu Kingdom's founding
Reception of Chinese imperial envoys to the Ryukyuan royal court
Victory ceremony after defeating a Japanese invasion
New Year festival at Shuri Castle
quiz.explanation: Kumiodori was created by Tamagusuku Chokun in 1719 to entertain Chinese imperial envoys (冊封使) visiting the Ryukyuan royal court — showcasing Okinawan high culture to representatives of the Ming/Qing court.

laws.title: Okinawa Duty-Free Shopping — Naha Airport Zone
laws.subtitle: Naha Airport Free Trade Zone enables tax-free commerce
laws.fullDescription: Naha Airport's Free Trade Zone (那覇空港自由貿易地域) allows duty-free import, processing, and re-export of goods — primarily cosmetics, fashion, electronics, and food products destined for mainland Japan or international markets. Goods sold within the free trade zone are exempt from Japanese customs duties but must exit Japan within the zone's framework. The zone supports Okinawa's hub-logistics strategy between East Asia and Japan's domestic market.
laws.penalty: Goods diverted from free trade zone into Japanese domestic market without customs declaration: full duty assessment + 30% penalty; deliberate smuggling: criminal customs violations
exceptions: Samples below de minimis value for legitimate trade promotion
laws.sourceLabel: Okinawa Prefecture — Naha Free Trade Zone

quiz.q: What strategic positioning does Naha Airport's Free Trade Zone leverage for Okinawa's economy?
options: Proximity to Tokyo for fast domestic logistics
Hub location between East Asia and Japan's domestic market
Deep port facilities for container shipping
quiz.explanation: Naha Airport's Free Trade Zone exploits Okinawa's geographic position between East Asia (China, Taiwan, Korea) and Japan's domestic market — enabling duty-free processing and redistribution of goods.

laws.title: Henoko Offshore Landfill — Marine Safety Zone
laws.subtitle: Construction zone enforced as restricted marine area
laws.fullDescription: The Henoko-Oura Bay offshore landfill construction site — for the new US Marine Corps air station — is designated a restricted marine area under the Coast Guard Act. Protest boats and kayakers approaching within the exclusion zone are intercepted by Japan Coast Guard vessels. The exclusion zone has been the site of the most physically confrontational interactions between protesters and authorities in modern Okinawan history. Coast Guard staff have been disciplined for excessive force; protesters have been criminally charged for zone entry.
laws.penalty: Entering Henoko marine exclusion zone without authorisation: coast guard removal + potential obstruction charges; repeat offenders: criminal prosecution
exceptions: Authorised research and construction vessels

quiz.q: What mode of protest transport has been most commonly used by activists challenging the Henoko marine exclusion zone?
quiz.explanation: Anti-base activists most commonly use kayaks and canoes to enter the Henoko marine exclusion zone in protest — allowing them to navigate the shallow bay waters and approach the construction site despite coast guard interception.

laws.title: Yambaru National Park — Biodiversity Protection
laws.subtitle: 2021 UNESCO World Natural Heritage — Japan's southernmost
laws.fullDescription: Yambaru (やんばる) — the forested northern Okinawa Peninsula — was inscribed as part of the Amami-Okinawa UNESCO World Natural Heritage in 2021, alongside the Amami Islands, Tokunoshima, Iriomote, and northern Okinawa. The inscription recognises outstanding endemic biodiversity including the Okinawa rail, Okinawa woodpecker, and Okinawa spiny rat. The Yambaru National Park (2016) governs access with Special Protection Zones restricting entry. Eco-tourism operators require prefecture licences.
laws.penalty: Unlicensed eco-tourism in Yanbaru National Park: fines up to ¥500,000; collection of plants or animals in Special Protection Zone: criminal penalties
exceptions: Licenced researchers and traditional forest users
laws.sourceLabel: Ministry of Environment — Yambaru National Park

quiz.q: When was the Amami-Okinawa UNESCO World Natural Heritage — including Yambaru — inscribed?
quiz.explanation: The Amami-Okinawa UNESCO World Natural Heritage was inscribed in July 2021 — recognising the extraordinary biodiversity of the Ryukyu island chain's subtropical forests and endemic species.

laws.title: Beach Resort Fee Transparency
laws.subtitle: Okinawa resort beach charges must be clearly disclosed
laws.fullDescription: Okinawa's premium resort hotels charge beach access, parasol rental, and water sport fees that sometimes surprise domestic and international visitors. Under the Act on Specified Commercial Transactions and Consumer Affairs Agency guidance, all fee structures must be clearly displayed — 'surprise charges' for beach amenities not disclosed at booking constitute deceptive trade practices. Okinawa Consumer Affairs Centre receives annual complaints about undisclosed resort fees during peak summer season.
laws.penalty: Undisclosed fees at point of booking: Consumer Affairs cease-and-desist; systematic deception: fines up to 3% of related revenue
exceptions: Voluntary tips and gratuities — standard in some international resorts — are not regulated
laws.sourceLabel: Consumer Affairs Agency — Tourism Fee Transparency

quiz.q: What consumer law principle requires Okinawa resort hotels to clearly disclose beach and amenity fees?
options: Act on Specified Commercial Transactions — fee structures must be clearly displayed at point of booking
Hotel Industry Standard Disclosure Rules only
quiz.explanation: Japan's Act on Specified Commercial Transactions requires all fee structures to be clearly disclosed — including resort beach access and amenity fees — before consumers commit to booking.

laws.title: Okinawa Peace Declaration — Annual Government Statement
laws.subtitle: Governor's annual June 23 peace message has legal basis
laws.fullDescription: The Okinawa Governor's Peace Declaration (平和宣言), delivered annually on June 23 (Okinawa Memorial Day), is a formal government statement calling for the abolition of nuclear weapons, reform of SOFA, and reduction of the US base burden. Under Okinawa's Memorial Day Ordinance, this is a required official act of the prefectural government. The 2023 Declaration specifically called for Japan to accede to the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW) — contrary to national government policy, creating a formal prefecture-nation policy conflict.
laws.penalty: N/A — this is a protected government speech act; the Governor's declarations have diplomatic implications but no domestic criminal dimension

quiz.q: What international treaty did Okinawa's 2023 Peace Declaration call on Japan to join — contrary to national government policy?
options: Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW)
quiz.explanation: Okinawa's 2023 Peace Declaration called on Japan to join the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW) — a treaty Japan has refused to sign as it would conflict with US extended nuclear deterrence commitments.
